nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What does environmental concern encompass according to Dunlap & Michelson (2002)?
nodes.answer: Environmental concern encompasses awareness of environmental issues, understanding the complexities of ecosystems, recognizing the human impact on the environment, and active engagement to preserve and restore it.
nodes.paragraph: And, specifically, among the teaching body and pre-service teachers, who will promote their students contact with nature and future attitudes of respect for it. The NEP-R scale is one of the most widely used instruments to measure ecological awareness and the degree of environmental concern in adult individuals. Environ - mental concern represents the extent to which people are aware of environmental issues and shows their readiness to personally contribute to solving them (Dunlap & Michelson, 2002 ). According to these authors, environmental concern goes beyond the individual S relationship with nature itself; it means understanding the complexi - ties of ecosystems and the impact of humans on the environment, as well as active engagement to preserve and restore it. The NEP-R scale has been widely used at the international level and in different sociodemographic contexts, mainly in European and American countries. Hawcroft and Milfont ( 2010 ) performed a meta-analysis of 69 scientific articles where the NEP scale had been used, drafted in 26 countries around the world, and highlighted that the scale S ecocentric dimension positively correlates with individuals pro-ecological behaviours.

nodes.label: Ethics and Regulation
nodes.question: Why do individuals believe in the obligation to prevent environmental damage?
nodes.answer: Individuals believe in the obligation to prevent environmental damage because they think all living things should survive equally, and that misbehavior can adversely affect others.

nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What was the catalyst for the evolution of environmental ethics?
nodes.answer: The evolution of environmental ethics was first witnessed in the early 1970s when proactive action was taken to protect the environment due to the increasing recognition of the moral relationships between ecosystems and human beings.

nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How does environmental ethics help clarify the existence of humans in nature?
nodes.answer: Environmental ethics helps clarify the existence of humans in nature by highlighting the interconnectedness between living things in the ecosystem and the environment, emphasizing the importance of sustainability and responsible utilization.
